balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For WH Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings. Non-controlling interests (minority shareholders' share of equity) jumped from $700m (FY2024) to $1,618m (FY2025) after Smithfield Foods' separate listing -- Smithfield went from ~100% owned to ~87-89% owned via its Jan-2025 IPO and Sep-2025 secondary offering, so a slice of consolidated equity that used to be WH Group's now belongs to Smithfield's public minority.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions
  • NCI growing as a share of total equity post-Smithfield IPO

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For WH Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For WH Group Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For WH Group Limited: only EPS is charted here -- WH Group reports its financials in USD but declares dividends in HKD (its listing currency), so there is no single-currency DPS figure in the statutory accounts. FY2025's dividend was HK$0.61/share, up from HK$0.50 in FY2024 (see the KPI card above); converting it into USD to sit beside EPS would mix a reporting currency with a declaration currency.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • HKD dividend growth versus USD earnings growth -- HKD/USD is pegged, but the mismatch is a reporting quirk worth knowing about

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For WH Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For WH Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For WH Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For WH Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom. WH Group's income statement also splits net income before/after fair-value marks on livestock (biological assets): FY2025 net income before bio-FV was $1,591m versus $1,915m statutory -- the $324m gap is a non-cash hog-price mark, not packaged-meats/pork cash profit, and it swings both ways year to year (before-FV was the larger number in FY2023 and FY2024).

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)
  • Net income before bio-FV vs statutory net income -- a widening gap is hog-price noise, not operating performance

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For WH Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For WH Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
